question: In July 2025, the Commission issued a reasoned opinion in infringement procedure INFR(2021)4052, requesting Spain to comply with EU rules on public procurement, including concession contracts. The Spanish Government had extended the duration of the concession for the AP-9 motorway by 25 years and sold it without initiating a tendering procedure.

According to Directive 2014/24/EU and the principles of equal treatment and transparency underlying EU public procurement rules, such an extension constitutes a substantial modification equivalent to the award of a new concession and requires a competitive tendering procedure. Spain had two months to respond and rectify the situation.

However, it has not carried out a competitive tendering procedure, has rejected the Commission’s position and has refused to comply with the reasoned opinion. The Supreme Court has now requested the Commission to clarify whether access to the reasoned opinion is legally permissible.
This raises questions regarding transparency and access to the documents exchanged between the Commission and Spain during the procedure. 1.

Can the Commission provide access to the response submitted by the Spanish Government to the reasoned opinion, in particular the document in which it rejected or declined to comply with the Commission’s request?
What is the current status of the infringement procedure and what further steps does the Commission intend to take in response to Spain’s refusal to comply with the reasoned opinion?
answer: As indicated in the reply to Written Question E-003666/2025 (1) raised by the Honourable Member, the Commission is bound to maintain the confidentiality of the content of an ongoing infringement procedure and cannot share details about it, with a view to attaining an appropriate solution.
This obligation applies to all the documents in an ongoing infringement procedure, including the replies from the Member State concerned.

Taking into account this obligation and based on the objective of protecting the purpose of the investigation under Regulation 1049/2001/EC (2), the Commission has refused granting public access to the documents pertaining to infringement procedure INFR(2021)4052 (3) following several requests lodged under that regulation.

To date, the Commission has not received any request from the Supreme Court regarding infringement procedure INFR(2021)4052. A request from a judicial authority of a Member State to gain privileged access, as opposed to public access, to documents held by the EU institutions is in principle to be treated pursuant to the principle of sincere cooperation laid down in Article 4(3) of the Treaty on European Union (4).
